prize_parts.citation: For the development of halide perovskite absorbers into efficient solution-processed solar cells.

statement.case_for: Halide perovskites took a chemically simple, solution-processable material class from a sensitizer in a dye cell (Miyasaka, 2009) to a solid-state device with lasting operation (Park, 2012) and to thin-film and planar architectures (Snaith), reaching certified efficiencies above 25 percent in about a decade. The work is clearly chemical (composition tuning, defect chemistry, interfaces), has been reproduced by thousands of groups, and bears directly on energy conversion, which is a central problem in chemistry. A three-name prize captures the three decisive steps: first demonstration, first durable solid-state cell, and the high-efficiency thin-film route.
statement.case_against: Credit is spread over more than three people. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have strong claims that a trio leaves out. Long-term stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing are unresolved, so a prize could be seen as early for the technology even if the science is mature. Of the shortlisted candidates, B005 also has narrower support than B020 and a lower first-place count, so it is not the consensus candidate.

responses.point: Linke ranks B020 first for its original chemical logic (catalytic, event-driven destruction of targets), and ranks B014 second, favouring a clean Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair.
responses.response: I agree B020 is a new pharmacological principle, and it is my second choice. My reservation is attribution. A trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli omits the cereblon and thalidomide mechanism (Handa, Ito), which is arguably the strongest mechanistic result and the one that explains drugs already used in patients. A prize that splits PROTACs from molecular glues would need two parts and still exclude Sakamoto, Kim and Gray. Clinical validation by an approved PROTAC is also still absent. On B014 I accept the two-name core, but the field has parallel platforms (454, Ion Torrent, Solexa), and the prize would still read more as a technology than as a chemical discovery.

responses.point: Aili ranks B020 first as a new therapeutic modality built on induced proximity, with Ciulli's structure-guided VHL design making degraders drug-like.
responses.response: I accept that structure-guided design was needed to make degraders drug-like, and it is a real chemical contribution. But it is a refinement of a concept already proved by Crews and Deshaies, and the molecular-glue strand with the cereblon mechanism has a separate and equally strong claim. I would rather see Handa on the list than Ciulli if only three names are allowed. I do not think timing is a strong objection to B020, but the absence of an approved degrader makes me less confident than you that it is ready this year.

responses.point: Åqvist ranks B053 (Car and Parrinello) first, as a clean two-person, long-established and overdue methodological advance, and gives B005 only eighth place for stability and credit reasons.
responses.response: The Car-Parrinello case is clean on attribution, and I agree it is mature. My difficulty is the committee's purpose: a method that is now background infrastructure sits against a discovery that created a new field of materials chemistry. I take your point about stability and the contested three-way split for B005, and I share it. Still, I think independent certification of efficiencies and the speed of adoption show impact that is at least as large, and the defect and composition chemistry is not just device engineering. B053 deserves a place among the strongest candidates, but I do not rank it above B005.

responses.point: Zou ranks B044 (molecular sieves) first and B015 second, and places B005 third, noting that stability and scale-up are open for the application but not for the discovery.
responses.response: I agree with your distinction between the discovery and the application, and it is the main reason I do not regard B005 as premature. We differ on B044. The zeolite field is broad and its credit is diffuse across synthesis, structure-directing agents and industrial catalysis, so a three-name prize would struggle to be clearly motivated. The 2025 framework-materials prize also reduces the room for another materials-synthesis award this soon.

uncertainties: Which three of Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok best represent the decisive contributions, and whether the supplied list omits an early originator.
Whether operational stability and lead toxicity make recognition of perovskites early relative to B020 or B014.
Whether B020 can be split fairly between PROTACs and molecular glues with at most three names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, but no shortlisted candidate has a documented connection to me; my own research area, biological energy conversion, is not a shortlisted topic.
